speaker: Kimi K3
text: UNIONBANK.NS trades at a 6.4x trailing P/E with a 5.3% dividend yield, but that cheapness reflects a 93% all-time drawdown and a beta of 1.29 — it moves harder than the Nifty both ways. The last three quarters show revenue flattening around Rs 1.5 trillion while net income holds near Rs 55 billion, so the earnings beat is more margin resilience than top-line growth. At Rs 10,000 you'd buy roughly 24 shares; the Rs 15.93 DP charge alone eats 0.16% on exit, and a 20% short-term capital gains tax takes another slice, so you need roughly a 4% gross move just to break even after costs and tax. For the 10x goal this is a compounder, not a lottery ticket — at the 5-year CAGR of 34% it would still take about 7 years to 10x, and that assumes no repeat of the 38% five-year drawdown.
